phase_name: Generalize Contention Tagging to Every Gate's Timeout Kill

objectives.description: _greg_load_1min helper and _greg_pool_job entry/kill load sampling (concurrent path)
verify-deploy.sh generic per-gate loop: sequential-path sampling, [CONTENTION] WARN-FINDING emission
New test suite test-gate-contention-tagging.sh, 8 cases (sequential + pool paths)
Declare new suite; fix a fourth latent fixture gap (test-orchestrate-unwind-dispatch.sh)

approaches_tried.approach: Sample entry/kill loadavg inside gate_registry_exec_bounded itself
approaches_tried.reason: That function cannot see a per-id output path for the sequential call site (a bare mktemp file, not a $dir/out.$id-shaped one) and runs inside a backgrounded subprocess under the concurrent-pool call site, where a plain global-variable write would never propagate back to the caller. Moved the sampling to both call sites instead (_greg_pool_job, and verify-deploy.sh's own generic per-gate loop), which already know their own id/outcome.

deviations.description: Reuse Gate 8's mutex-wait fraction signal generically, alongside the load threshold
deviations.reason: The mutex-wait signal is intrinsically specific to Gate 8's own specs/.gate-lock acquire; most of the other 30 gates never touch that mutex at all, so there is no generic analog to generalize. Only the load-threshold signal was generalized; stated explicitly rather than silently narrowed.
deviations.annotation: *(deviation: altered — load-only generalization, mutex-wait fraction left gate-8-specific)*

notes: lint-fixture-dependency-declaration.sh caught a FOURTH fixture suite (test-orchestrate-unwind-dispatch.sh) needing the same batch-gate-marker-lib.sh fixture-copy fix already applied in Phases 4/5 to test-orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh, test-orchestrate-batch-gate.sh, and test-force-phases.sh. The lint's own full-corpus scan after each phase's edits has been the reliable way to find every such gap -- recommended as a standing habit after any new orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh dependency.

The new suite deliberately builds on gate_store_fixture_build (already proven by test-gate-registry-resolution.sh's case35-39) rather than a from-scratch fixture, post-editing the generated row's timeout_s and function body (sed-replacing the generated 'pass ... (fixture)' line with a deliberate stall) -- cheap (8 cases run in well under a minute) and exercises the real verify-deploy.sh dispatch loop rather than a synthetic registry bypass.
